This project is academic, not a regulated deployment. It adopts the structure
of institutional model risk management anyway, on the three-component standard:
**conceptual soundness**, **ongoing monitoring**, **outcomes analysis**.

## 14.1 Model card

`MODEL_CARD.md`, regenerated per version, with the artefact registered in
`models/registry.json` under its content hash. Version history:

| version | trained | n_train | n_test | threshold | XGB AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-1.0.0-real | 2026-10-27 | 13242 | 4830 | 0.3250 | 0.9589 |

Two of the three versions exist because a defect was found and corrected, and
both corrections **lowered** the headline number:

- **v1.0.0 → v1.1.0** — financial-sector issuers were in training in violation
  of §5.6. Their test rows carried 8.5% prevalence against 22.7% elsewhere and
  scored AUC 0.9888, flattering the aggregate without the model understanding
  a single bank.
- **v1.1.0 → v1.2.0** — `log_mkt_cap` and `equity_volatility` were look-ahead.
  `CUR_MKT_CAP` and `VOLATILITY_260D` are real-time Bloomberg market fields and
  ignore the `EQY_FUND_YEAR` override, so every historical row carried the
  pull-date value (98.4% and 95.4% of tickers held one value across eleven
  years). See `MODEL_CARD.md` §5b.

A validation record whose metrics only ever improve is not recording
validation.

## 14.2 Conceptual soundness

**Theoretical basis.** The feature set follows the distress literature's four
channels — liquidity (working capital, current ratio), profitability (ROA,
EBIT/assets, retained earnings/assets), leverage, and coverage — operationalised
as Altman's Z-score family and extended with temporal deltas. The §8.1 model
hierarchy is reported in full rather than by winner: a benchmark (Altman Z″),
a statistical baseline (L2 logistic), and the primary model (XGBoost).

**The assumption the model rests on, stated plainly.** The label is a §7.5
*financial-criteria distress proxy*, not a realised default. Agency ratings
resolved for 4 of 3,000 tickers (0.13%) — CRISIL returns `#N/A Authorization`
on 2,999 — so the ratings-based label in §7.2 was unavailable as a matter of
data entitlement. **Every performance figure in this report is conditional on
that proxy.**

**Where the theory had to be overruled by measurement.** Canonical Altman Z″
is *circular* under this label: its X4 term is equity/liabilities, and
`sign(X4) == (book equity < 0)` on 100.00% of rows, which is label criterion 2
exactly. The feature set therefore uses the three-term `altman_z_ex_x4`, while
canonical Z″ is retained as the §8.1 benchmark. Circularity is enforced in
code by `assert_no_circular_leak()`, not by review.

**The conditions under which the model fails**, enumerated in `MODEL_CARD.md`
§9 (13 limitations) and summarised here: financial-sector balance sheets
(excluded, §5.6); firms with over half their features null (reported as
unscoreable, not scored low); Real Estate, the weakest sector at AUC 0.8745;
and any reading of the output as a calibrated probability (§14.4 below).

**Block attribution confirms the model is doing what the theory says.**

| block | share_pct | n_features |
|---|---|---|
| block3_profitability | 64.7400 | 3 |
| block5_zscore | 12.4767 | 5 |
| block2_liquidity | 8.2914 | 3 |
| block6_temporal | 7.7532 | 2 |
| block7_controls | 6.7386 | 1 |

It is overwhelmingly a profitability model, which is the substantive answer to
"what does this add over Altman": it weights current earnings power far above
Altman's fixed 1968 coefficients.

## 14.3 Ongoing monitoring

Implemented in `src/monitoring.py`; full output in
`reports/phase7/MONITORING.md`. Reference window FY2014-FY2020 (train),
current FY2022-FY2023 (test).

| name | status | value | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| feature_drift | watch | 0.1430 | 2/14 features at PSI >= 0.25; worst is consecutive_loss_years at 0.4295 |
| missingness_rise | ok | 0.0500 | altman_z_ex_x4 non-reporting rose +0.1pp (3.8% -> 3.9%) |
| performance_decay | ok | -0.0201 | early-warning AUC 0.9244 -> 0.9445 (-0.0201) on 169 events |
| prediction_shift | ok | 0.0220 | mean predicted probability 0.3101 -> 0.3032 (+2.2% relative) |
| prevalence_shift | ok | 0.1870 | base rate 27.90% -> 22.70% (+19% relative) on 4,340 rows; the §8.4 threshold was chosen at the former |

**Retrain recommended: False.**

All four §14.3 requirements are implemented as *triggers with thresholds*, not
as charts:

- **Feature drift** — PSI per feature, with **missingness bucketed
  explicitly**. The usual non-null-only implementation scores a feature that
  went from 5% to 60% null at 0.00; in a distress panel that is the signal, not
  noise, because firms under stress stop filing.
- **Performance decay** — measured on the **early-warning stratum**, not the
  pooled AUC. The label persists 89.8% year over year, so pooled AUC would mask
  a total collapse in the model's actual job.
- **Prediction distribution shift** — mean predicted probability between
  refreshes, tracked separately from feature drift because they fail
  independently; a moving output centre with stable inputs is what a
  mis-versioned artefact looks like from outside.
- **Retraining trigger** — any trigger firing opens a **human review**, never
  an automatic retrain (§14.5). The review's first question is whether the
  drift is a pipeline fault, because in this project's history it was the
  pipeline more often than the market.

A status of `insufficient` is **not** a pass. It records that the evidence to
decide was absent, which is itself a monitoring finding.

## 14.4 Outcomes analysis

Implemented in `src/outcomes_analysis.py`; full output in
`reports/phase7/OUTCOMES_ANALYSIS.md`.

At the §8.4 operating threshold of **0.245**, the model produced
**24 false negatives** against 985 realised events
(97.6% recall). §14.4 requires each one to be reviewed
individually, and each was, against the **training window's** distribution:

| verdict | n | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| SIGNAL ABSENT | 12 | nothing available sat in a historically adverse tail — a limit of the data |
| SIGNAL UNUSED | 11 | something did, and the model scored through it — a limit of the model |
| DATA MISSING | 1 | over half the features null; unscoreable in substance |

Per-case detail, with the specific adverse features named, is in
`reports/phase7/false_negative_review.csv`.

### The finding this section exists to surface

**The model is systematically over-confident and its output must not be read
as a probability.** Decile calibration gives a mean gap of **−0.175** across
deciles 7–10; decile 8 predicts 69.8% against a realised 45.2%. The cause is
`scale_pos_weight`, which inflates predicted probabilities by construction.

Ranking is unaffected — AUC, KS and the operating threshold are rank
statistics, and the threshold was chosen on validation under the same
distortion — so the flag/no-flag decision is sound. But a user reading "70%"
is being misinformed. Either the interface presents the score as a risk
**rank** (which §12.3's bands already do) or a calibration layer fitted on the
validation window only is added before any probability is quoted.

---

## 14.5 Human-in-the-loop

**Non-negotiable.** CRESTA produces analytical estimates, never automated
decisions. No credit, lending or investment action may be taken on a model
output without qualified human review. This is enforced in three places rather
than asserted once:

- every API prediction carries a disclaimer and its `model_version`;
- every CSV export is stamped with model version, config hash, commit,
  timestamp, threshold and the §14.5 constraint;
- a fired monitoring trigger opens a review; it cannot ship a model.

## Headline results, for the record

| model | n_scored | auc_roc | pr_auc | ks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Persistence (label at t)  [naive baseline] | 4340 | 0.8859 | 0.7109 | 0.7718 |
| Altman Z'' (benchmark) | 4172 | 0.7729 | 0.6592 | 0.4888 |
| Altman Z'' @ conventional 1.1 cutoff | 4172 | 0.7729 | 0.6592 | 0.4888 |
| Logistic regression (L2, balanced) | 4340 | 0.8742 | 0.6655 | 0.6826 |
| XGBoost | 4340 | 0.9507 | 0.8315 | 0.7819 |

**The pooled number is not the headline.** The §7.5 label is identical at *t*
and *t+1* on 89.8% of rows, so a naive "the condition continues" baseline
scores AUC 0.8859 by itself. Against that baseline:

- **Altman Z″ (0.7729) is significantly WORSE than no model at all**
  (ΔAUC −0.1110, DeLong p < 1e-300).
- The logistic baseline is **not significantly different** from persistence.
- Only XGBoost beats it (0.9507, ΔAUC +0.0648, p < 1e-300).

Reporting only the Altman comparison — the convention in this literature —
would have been materially misleading.

### Stability across five rolling origins

| fold | test_year | persistence | altman | logistic | xgboost | altman_EW | logistic_EW | xgboost_EW |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2019 | 0.8504 | 0.7642 | 0.8929 | 0.9307 | 0.6569 | 0.8573 | 0.9094 |
| 2 | 2020 | 0.8817 | 0.7562 | 0.8671 | 0.9343 | 0.6203 | 0.8292 | 0.9242 |
| 3 | 2021 | 0.9036 | 0.7732 | 0.8518 | 0.9449 | 0.6909 | 0.8014 | 0.9184 |
| 4 | 2022 | 0.8800 | 0.7661 | 0.8671 | 0.9502 | 0.6364 | 0.8241 | 0.9455 |
| 5 | 2023 | 0.8924 | 0.7800 | 0.8913 | 0.9540 | 0.6966 | 0.8656 | 0.9445 |

The single-split headline sits inside one standard deviation of the fold mean,
so it is a representative draw rather than a favourable one.

## Track B (ESG) — validated as infeasible, not deferred

`reports/phase6/track_b_feasibility.md`. BRSR is mandatory only from FY2022-23
and the panel's last feature year *is* FY2022-23, so ESG exists for exactly one
feature year and invariant 2 forbids the random split an A-vs-B test would
need: **no out-of-time ESG comparison exists in this data.** The eligible frame
carries 4.3 events per variable against a ≥10 rule of thumb. A seven-filing
extraction pilot met its coverage gate at 77.9% but **only 1 of 7 filings
disclosed enough to form the energy-intensity ratio §6.8 specifies** — the
renewable split is a voluntary *Leadership* indicator.

This is a finding about the disclosure regime, not about ESG.

## Open items a reviewer should know about

- **`CUR_MKT_CAP` / `VOLATILITY_260D` need a `BDH` re-pull** to restore two
  legitimate market features removed as look-ahead
  (`Data_Extraction_Guide_v2.md` Part 2.3). `tests/test_no_lookahead.py` will
  fail by design when that pull lands, telling whoever does it that the
  exclusion can be lifted.
- **The cost ratio is an assumption and a consequential one.** §8.4's default
  10:1 FN:FP drives the threshold toward flagging a large share of the
  portfolio; 3:1 maximises F1. The deployed ratio must be stated wherever a
  flag is shown.
- **LightGBM comparator not installed**; Bloomberg DRSK not used as a third
  benchmark.
- **Provenance is shallow.** The repository was initialised at Phase 3, so the
  config hash and commit pin the current state but carry no history of how the
  pipeline reached it.
